policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'Herod, king of Judaea' renders the appositive with no exponent for a Greek article before basileus; both readings yield identical English.
ASV reads 'and he had a wife of the daughters of Aaron' with an indefinite 'a wife'; the RP reading kai he gyne autou would give the definite-possessive 'and his wife was of the daughters of Aaron'.
ASV 'he had a wife' renders the dative of possession auto; the genitive autou would be rendered 'his wife was of the daughters of Aaron'.
ASV 'righteous before God' renders either enantion or enopion identically; no note is mapped here.
Word order only; ASV 'because that Elisabeth was barren' does not reflect Greek constituent order.
ASV 'at his birth' renders genesei and gennesei alike.
Presence or absence of the article with kyriou is not distinguished by ASV 'in the sight of the Lord'.
Word order only; ASV 'while he tarried in the temple' does not reflect the position of auton. The mapped notes are alternative_rendering and cannot decide a reading.
Augment spelling edynato/edynato with eta; ASV 'he could not speak' renders both alike.
Article before kyrios only; ASV 'hath the Lord done' is the same either way.
Article before oneidos only; ASV 'my reproach' is the same either way.
ASV 'was sent from God' renders apo tou theou; hypo would give agency, 'sent by God'.
Reduplication spelling only; ASV 'betrothed' renders either form.
ASV 'And he came in unto her, and said' has no subject noun; the addition ho angelos would be rendered 'the angel came in unto her'.

ASV ends the greeting at 'the Lord is with thee' and relegates the longer text to a textual_variant note, 'Many ancient authorities add blessed art thou among women' - so the addition is not the text rendered.
ASV 'she was greatly troubled at the saying' has no exponent for RP's idousa ('when she saw him') and no possessive for autou ('his saying').
Feminine/common-gender spelling of the same noun; ASV 'thy kinswoman' renders both.
Finite verb versus periphrastic participle; ASV 'she also hath conceived a son' is the natural English of either.
ASV 'no word from God' renders para tou theou with the genitive; para to theo (dative) would be rendered 'with God' ('nothing shall be impossible with God').
Word order of the subject relative to the object phrase; ASV 'when Elisabeth heard the salutation of Mary' follows English order and does not witness the Greek sequence.
ASV 'lifted up her voice with a loud cry' renders kraugei as 'cry' (the 'voice' rendering anephonesen); phonei megalei would give 'with a loud voice'.
Emphatic versus enclitic pronoun; ASV 'unto me' renders both alike.
Word order only; ASV 'the babe leaped in my womb for joy' follows English order.
ASV 'great things' renders megala and megaleia alike.
ASV 'unto generations and generations' renders the coordinated kai geneas; RP's genitive chain geneon would give 'from generation to generation'.
ASV 'about three months' renders hos and hosei alike.
Word order and article only; ASV 'on the eighth day' is the same either way.
ASV 'There is none of thy kindred that is called by this name' suits either ek tes syngeneias or en tei syngeneiai; the partitive 'of' is idiomatic English for both.
Gender of the pronoun only; ASV 'what he would have him called' renders both.
Article before onoma only; ASV 'His name is John' is the same either way.
ASV renders the connective explicitly: 'For the hand of the Lord was with him'; RP omits gar and would leave the clause asyndetic.
Augment placement in the same verb; ASV 'and prophesied' renders both.
Article before oiko only; ASV 'In the house' is the same either way.
Article before paidos autou only; ASV 'of his servant David' is the same either way.
Article with hagion only; ASV 'his holy prophets' is the same either way.
ASV 'out of the hand of our enemies' renders the possessive hemon, unitalicized and so not a supply; the base echthron alone would give 'of enemies'.
ASV 'all our days' has no exponent for RP's tes zoes; that reading would be rendered 'all the days of our life'.
ASV renders kai ... de with the double connective 'Yea and thou, child'; without de the clause would be simply 'And thou, child'.
ASV 'thou shalt go before the face of the Lord' renders pro prosopou with the noun 'face'; enopion would give simply 'before the Lord'.
ASV reads the future 'shall visit us' (episkepsetai) and puts the aorist in a textual_variant note, 'Many ancient authorities read hath visited us.'
